## Historical audit — S0097

**Scope:** Only chunk 7 of 7 is visible. All citations below refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/replay_s1_r1/M_initial/C1/replay_selection/commons_29206714/trajectory.jsonl`. Character ranges identify the supplied split observations; images themselves are not visible in this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Line 22, chars [419000,631433), step-2 feedback and student program | The inferred goal was to reconstruct a reference historic kitchen in editable 3D. The program defines multiple groups: architecture and hearth, cabinet with open doors, china, yarn winder, foreground wheel and spindle. These are code-level objects, not independent proof of their appearance. |
| Same range, student program | The student diagnosed the counter and shelves as too high and hypothesized an overly tall base. The submitted program scales the base to 0.82, extends the upper cabinet and contents around the crown, and moves the winder to the calculated counter surface. It also constructs a rim, spokes, hub and supports, rotates the wheel to −48 degrees, and notes possible plate occlusion. Actual contact and connections are not geometrically verified. |
| Same range, student program | The scene specifies wood, ceramic, metal and other colors, glass opacity, plaster-wear geometry, global roughness, a camera and two area lights. This establishes intended finishes and setup, not texture fidelity or proof that lighting and camera match the reference. The door and wheel angles are specified poses; their visible correctness is unknown. |
| Same range, step-2 and step-3 execution feedback | Step 2 was reported usable. The submitted complete program then produced step 3: `ok: true`, 16/16 samples, saved PNG and blend file, empty stderr, and `usable_render: true`. This is **formal render success**, not visual or geometric validation. The execution budget was exhausted; no further revision could run. |
| Same range, feedback and final-selection instruction; lines 23–25, chars [0,6352), [0,362), [0,59) | The student was instructed to compare reference and renders, check openings, supports and materials, preserve unrelated groups, and select a successful step. The visible program implements checks and changes consistent with that instruction, but no separately identified teacher message or teacher diagnosis is visible; teacher receipt or adoption cannot be established. The final read-only student session had no tool calls and returned `SELECT 3`; a subsequent `select` event recorded step 3. |

**Exploration and outcome.** The record reports successful steps 1–3 and shows one autonomous revision and final selection, but earlier exploration is outside this chunk. The nonempty program executed successfully; there is no visible algorithm failure, empty patch, or technical interruption. Overall reconstruction correctness remains **unknown**, not formal visual success or verified partial correctness. Selection of step 3 is the student’s choice, not independent evidence that it is best.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, separating an observed discrepancy from its causal hypothesis and moving dependent contents with a transformed support makes dependencies explicit. Task-specific hypotheses here are that base height caused the shelf mismatch and wheel azimuth hid an existing opening. Both were changed in the same execution, limiting attribution; neither is independently verified. The reference and renders, earlier teacher interactions, actual surface quality, occlusion, support contact, framing and lighting quality remain unavailable to this audit.
